newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Indonesia expected to lift Australia meat ban soon.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia expected to lift Australia meat ban soon.

text.p: Indonesia was expected to remove its ban on the import of Australian meat from the state of New South Wales (NSW) because of anthrax scares very soon, the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp (AMLC) said on Thursday.
"We think they will be lifted very shortly, probably in the next week or so," Peter Barnard, general manager policy, planning and public affairs at the AMLC, told Reuters.
He described the ban, which followed a significant outbreak of anthrax in Victoria in January and unrelated minor subsequent outbreaks in NSW, as largely the result of a misunderstanding.
Indonesia's Department of Agriculture said last week it had lifted its ban on meat imports from the state of Victoria.
This followed a March 26 declaration by Australia's federal Primary Industries Minister John Anderson that the Victorian anthrax outbreak was officially over.

Australian officials have said that the Indonesian ban on imports of meat from NSW, imposed on March 10, was mistaken because outbreaks of the disease in this state were isolated, few and effectively insignificant.
Barnard said Australia's major meat industry trade with Indonesia was in 400,000 head a year of live cattle.
This, the equivalent of 70,000 tonnes of beef, left from Australia's north and was unaffected by the ban, he said.
Only about 5,000 tonnes of Australian meat exports to Indonesia were from affected areas, he said.
"This puts the whole problem in perspective. Out of (Australia's) total meat exports of about 700,000 tonnes, only less than 5,000 tonnes is affected by this problem," he said.
Meetings had been held with Indonesian authorities in an attempt to resolve the misunderstanding, he said.
Australia exported a total of 738,000 tonnes of beef and veal, worth A$2.39 billion, in 1995/96 (July-June).
